title: Projection of FY2023 Tax Revenue Growth and Impact on Additional Help for Singaporeans to Deal with Inflationary Costs
what_it_is: Projection of FY2023 Tax Revenue Growth and Impact on Additional Help for Singaporeans to Deal with Inflationary Costs

sections.label: Tax revenue and Assurance Package
sections.summary: Higher FY2022 tax revenue came from post-COVID economic recovery; MOF is studying further Assurance Package enhancements and will announce details shortly.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The higher tax revenue collection in financial year 2022 (FY2022), compared to the previous year, was due to our economic recovery after the COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: While some of this growth momentum has benefited tax revenue collections in FY2023, it is unclear whether the trend can continue due to the uncertain global economic outlook.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: The Government understands that cost of living remains a key concern.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: That is why we had enhanced the Assurance Package to $9.6 billion in Budget 2023 to provide Singaporeans with additional financial support.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: As Prime Minister Lee mentioned at the 2023 National Day Rally, the Ministry of Finance (MOF) is currently studying further enhancements to the Assurance Package.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Minister of State for Finance (Mr Chee Hong Tat) (for the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister for Finance)
sentences.text: We will announce more details shortly, after the review is completed.

sections.label: Tax collection momentum and cost of living
sections.summary: Tax collection reflects earlier economic activity, and the Government will study enhancing the Assurance Package to help with cost of living concerns.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: So, we collect the taxes, say, in a particular period, it actually refers to the economic activity several months back in a previous period.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: That is why I mentioned that the collection, there is a certain momentum that we are seeing even in the current financial year arising from the stronger economic performance and recovery post-COVID-19 pandemic.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But whether this can continue, this is something that we need to watch very carefully because, as Mr Ang would be aware, there are some dark clouds in the global economy and the economic outlook for this year is unlikely to be as strong as, say, last year.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: But, nevertheless, the point that I made in my main reply that we understand that there are cost of living concerns because that remains a concern for many Singaporean families and the Government will look at how we can provide more help.

sentences.speaker: Mr Chee Hong Tat
sentences.text: We will study whether there are ways to enhance the Assurance Package and, in particular, we have been providing not just vouchers but also cash components and many other types of assistance to Singaporeans within the Assurance Package and that is something that we will look at as well – how to channel the resources to provide the maximum impact.
